# Historical execution audit

**Provenance and citation convention.** All cited expanded files are under `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C2/`. Their corresponding archive is `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/work/scene_archive/bundles/r2--sceneevolve_cli.tar.gz`; the member is `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C2/` followed by the cited relative path. Line numbers refer to the original expanded files.

## Chaise room — development/commons_109923183

Step 2 constructs a paneled room, 132 individually colored and rotated parquet boards, and a chaise assembled from rounded boxes, swept-tube rails and legs, balls, a tilted back, segmented wings and a loose pillow. A foreground chair uses crossed rods for cane; curtains are box folds [X1217, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 25–64, 66–175]. These are modeled parts, not evidence that their surfaces physically connect.

The code sets material roughness to .76 and conditionally adds noise bump and a generated-coordinate Voronoi color ramp based on object names; the actual affected objects depend on realized names and material sharing [X1217, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 177–213]. Step 3 replaces the three wing sections per side with one panel, rotates the head −25° and pillow −35° about Z, and rotates and offsets the wall group. Its 68 mm lens replaces step 2’s 58 mm, with a raised target; both use two area lights and AgX [X1219, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 8–17, 52–54, 93–117, 136–141, 215–224; X1217, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 15–17].

The step 3 comments report step 2’s chaise image bounds as approximately (.14,.22)–(.77,.83), versus reference (.04,.24)–(.83,.93), and report seams and a mismatched wall boundary. These are author observations, not independently measured here [X1219, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 1–3]. The reference metadata is 512 × 384 [X1221, `task.json`, lines 2–5]. Steps 1–3 each report `ok: true`, no error or stderr, 16/16 samples, and saved PNG and blend files [X1216, `steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7; X1218, `steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7; X1220, `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7]. No chaise selection or acceptance record is supplied.

## Ship compartment — development/commons_118588033

The generated scene represents a 3.6 × 8.9 × 3.15 shell, stanchion, three box-built bunk tiers, lockers, protective rod frame, machinery, chair, pipes and fittings [X1230, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 8–103, 105–142]. Step 2 moves the bunks .25 in X and relocates the front lamp; step 3 retains that move, moves the lamp again and darkens floor, ceiling and ambient light [X1228, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 44–56, 148–151; X1230, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 4–6, 15–25, 41–52, 144–159].

The camera remains at (.12, −4.7, 1.69), lens 26 and sensor 32. Three lamp-associated area lights plus two fills, AgX, zero exposure and .73 Principled roughness are specified; no image texture operation is present in this build [X1230, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 9–12, 152–171]. Comments describe the preceding lamp at (.35,.21) versus reference (.39,.16), and a still-pale floor and ceiling; these are reported visual assessments, not verified images [X1230, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 4–6]. Reference metadata is 384 × 512 [X1232, `task.json`, lines 2–5].

All three step results report successful 16-sample renders and saved files, with empty stderr [X1227, `steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7; X1229, `steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7; X1231, `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7]. `selected.json` records step 3, although the record’s `selected` field is null [X1224, `selected.json`, line 2; X1223, `record.json`, line 57]. The record reports overall .41385 and functional passes for architecture, explicitly limited to structural/edit operability; semantic completeness and support/collision truth are null. Functional testing fell back to CPU because the authorized GPU became busy—not a recorded render failure [X1223, `record.json`, lines 16–34, 156–170].

## Kitchen — selection/commons_133800864

The supplied build uses box-and-rod cabinetry, blinds, towel folds, a Boolean-cut sink, tap, blender, pitcher and multipart jug. Granite receives noise/ramp coloring; chrome-matched materials receive metallic .8 and roughness .25. Camera lens is 49, with two area lights, Standard transform and exposure −1.15 [X1233, `build.py`, lines 24–58, 72–151, 162–199]. Comments report residual jug, roll and towel placement/appearance discrepancies; they do not establish final visual quality [X1233, `build.py`, lines 1–3].

The record says complete, three executions, no runtime error, overall .45403 and functional passes for appliances, again only structural/edit operability; contact and semantic completeness remain null [X1234, `record.json`, lines 16–34, 39–53]. A separate file records selection of step 3 [X1235, `selected.json`, line 2]. No individual kitchen execution log is supplied here, so the record does not independently establish its rendered appearance.

**Conclusion:** The supplied logs establish technical completion for the six chaise and ship renders, not fidelity. Recorded scores and functional acceptance are not independent visual validation; without images, physical contact and reconstruction quality remain unresolved.
